project.name: MediView - 45-Day MVP
project.description: The 45-day teaching cut of MediView. A patient self-registers and books inside a doctor's schedule; an admin simulates the x-ray import; a doctor opens the study in a Cornerstone.js viewport under a Redis single-writer lock, writes a report with medications and finalizes it; the Study status (To do -> In progress -> Re-diagnosis -> Done) is the single source of truth and closes over an integration event. Four .NET 10 microservices - Identity, Studies, Imaging, Reporting - plus a YARP gateway and a Blazor Server web app, 15 database tables, 8 pages. The full-product plan (11 deployables, 41 tables, 15 screens, Azure) is preserved in checklist.json and mediview.dbml; what was removed and why is in scope-cut.md.

techStack.architecture: DDD + Clean Architecture (Domain / Application / Infrastructure / Api) x 4 services + YARP gateway
techStack.database: PostgreSQL - 15 tables, one schema per service, FKs only inside a schema
techStack.cache: Redis (single-writer study lock: SET NX PX + Lua compare-and-delete)
techStack.messaging: MassTransit over RabbitMQ with the EF Core transactional outbox
techStack.cqrs: Hand-rolled dispatcher + Result<T> + FluentValidation - no MediatR dependency
techStack.auth: JWT access tokens + rotating refresh tokens, one role claim, three policies
techStack.orm: Entity Framework Core (Npgsql), snake_case, xmin concurrency - no Dapper in the MVP
techStack.imaging: fo-dicom parsing, blob-backed storage, WADO/QIDO-shaped endpoints, Cornerstone.js viewport
techStack.realtime: SignalR (announcements only; Redis is the lock authority)
techStack.storage: IBlobStore port with a local-disk adapter (Azure Blob is a same-shape swap)
techStack.testing: xUnit aggregate unit tests + Testcontainers integration tests + one e2e happy path
techStack.cloud: None in scope - runs entirely on docker compose. Azure deployment is deferred.

servicesCut: Role & Permission (replaced by one role column + 3 policies)
Booking (merged into Studies - an appointment exists only to produce a Study)
Prescription (collapsed into one child table on the Report aggregate)
Cart & Billing / Payment (an e-commerce sub-domain; teaches checkout, not imaging or DDD)
Notification (SignalR toasts cover the demo; email/SMS adds infrastructure, not lessons)
tablesCut: billing.* (7): carts, cart_items, wallets, bills, bill_items, payments, wallet_transactions
identity role matrix (3): roles, permissions, role_permissions, user_roles
alsoCut: Azure infrastructure as code (Bicep) and production deployment
CI/CD beyond a build-and-test GitHub Actions workflow
The security & compliance programme (Key Vault, encryption at rest, GDPR tooling)
OpenTelemetry distributed tracing (Serilog + correlation id is kept)
Dapper read models (EF projection is enough at this data size)
The Redis SignalR backplane (single instance in the MVP)
UI screens: wallet, cart & checkout, follow-up booking, roles matrix, mobile layout

keptBecauseItTeaches.studies.studies + study_status_history: a rich aggregate root with a real state machine and an owned child collection
keptBecauseItTeaches.studies.study_locks + Redis: distributed single-writer concurrency - the differentiator of this project
keptBecauseItTeaches.reporting.reports + report_medications: a second aggregate, immutability after finalize, cross-service choreography
keptBecauseItTeaches.imaging.series + instances: the DICOM hierarchy and a blob-backed infrastructure adapter
keptBecauseItTeaches.studies.audit_log: break-glass - the healthcare-specific lesson, kept small

sections.name: Foundation & Shared Kernel
sections.goal: Days 1-3 - A compiling solution with the four-layer convention agreed and a tiny shared kernel (Entity, Result, domain events, error middleware) that all four services reuse. No MediatR: a 40-line dispatcher you write yourself teaches more and removes a licensed dependency.

tasks.title: Pin the .NET 10 SDK with global.json
tasks.details: Lock every machine and CI runner to the same SDK so `dotnet build` cannot behave differently on two boxes.
acceptanceCriteria: `dotnet --version` prints 10.x from the repo root
steps: Run `dotnet --list-sdks` and confirm a 10.x SDK is present.
At the repo root run `dotnet new globaljson --sdk-version 10.0.100 --roll-forward latestFeature`.
Commit global.json.

tasks.title: Create the solution skeleton and folder layout
tasks.details: src/BuildingBlocks, src/Services/{Identity,Studies,Imaging,Reporting}, src/Gateway, src/Web. Four projects per service: Domain / Application / Infrastructure / Api. Folders are named after domain concepts, never after patterns.
acceptanceCriteria: `dotnet build` succeeds on an empty 18-project solution
MediView.*.Domain.csproj has zero PackageReference entries
steps: Keep the existing MedicalView.sln; add solution folders BuildingBlocks, Services, Gateway, Web.
For each of the 4 services run 4 `dotnet new` commands (classlib x3 + web) named MediView.<Svc>.{Domain,Application,Infrastructure,Api}.
Wire the inward-only references: Application->Domain, Infrastructure->Application, Api->Infrastructure.
Add every project to the solution and run `dotnet build` - it must be green before you write a line of logic.

tasks.title: Central package management and shared build properties
tasks.details: Directory.Packages.props holds every version; Directory.Build.props turns on nullable, implicit usings and warnings-as-errors for all projects at once.
acceptanceCriteria: A version bump happens in exactly one file
steps: Confirm Directory.Build.props has Nullable, LangVersion latest, ImplicitUsings, TreatWarningsAsErrors.
Confirm Directory.Packages.props has ManagePackageVersionsCentrally=true.
Add the first PackageVersion entries as you need them - never a Version= on an individual PackageReference.

tasks.title: Add .editorconfig and analyzers
tasks.details: One formatting rule set so diffs are about logic. Enable the built-in .NET analyzers at a level you will actually keep green.
acceptanceCriteria: `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` passes
steps: Add a .editorconfig at the repo root (4-space C#, file-scoped namespaces, `var` where apparent).
Set EnforceCodeStyleInBuild and AnalysisLevel=latest-recommended in Directory.Build.props.
Run `dotnet format` once and commit the result as a formatting-only commit.

tasks.title: BuildingBlocks.Domain: Entity, AggregateRoot, domain events
tasks.details: The base types every aggregate inherits. AggregateRoot collects domain events in a private list and exposes them read-only - the pattern that keeps side effects out of the middle of a method.
acceptanceCriteria: A test aggregate can raise an event and expose it read-only
The project still has zero package references
steps: Create Entity<TId> with an Id and identity-based Equals/GetHashCode.
Create IDomainEvent (a marker record with OccurredOn) and AggregateRoot<TId> with `Raise(IDomainEvent)`, `IReadOnlyCollection<IDomainEvent> DomainEvents` and `ClearDomainEvents()`.
Create ValueObject with structural equality (or just use C# `record` - decide once and write it in the ADR).
Create DomainException, the base for every invariant violation.

tasks.title: BuildingBlocks.Application: Result<T> and a hand-rolled dispatcher
tasks.details: Result<T> for expected failures (exceptions only for the genuinely exceptional). Then ~40 lines of ICommand/IQuery + handler interfaces + a DI-resolved dispatcher, instead of taking a MediatR dependency. Writing it yourself is the lesson.
acceptanceCriteria: A sample command round-trips through the dispatcher in a unit test
No MediatR package reference anywhere in the solution
steps: Create Error(code, message) and Result / Result<T> with Success/Failure and an implicit conversion.
Define ICommand<TResponse>, IQuery<TResponse>, ICommandHandler<TCommand,TResponse>, IQueryHandler<,>.
Write ISender with `Send<TResponse>(IRequest<TResponse>)` that resolves the handler from IServiceProvider via a closed generic type lookup.
Add an AddApplication() extension that scans the assembly and registers every handler as scoped.

tasks.title: Validation and logging pipeline behaviours
tasks.details: Cross-cutting concerns wrap the handler so handlers stay pure domain logic.
acceptanceCriteria: An invalid command never reaches its handler
Every handled request produces one structured log line
steps: Add FluentValidation and a ValidationBehaviour that runs all validators for the request and returns a Failure result on the first error set.
Add a LoggingBehaviour that logs the request name, elapsed ms and outcome - structured, never interpolated.
Chain the behaviours in the dispatcher (a decorator list is enough; you do not need a pipeline framework).

tasks.title: Error handling middleware + correlation id
tasks.details: One place that turns domain failures into RFC-7807 ProblemDetails, so every service returns errors in the same shape.
acceptanceCriteria: A thrown DomainException returns 400 ProblemDetails with a correlation id
An unhandled exception never leaks a stack trace to the client
steps: Write CorrelationIdMiddleware: read or create X-Correlation-Id, push it into the Serilog log scope, echo it on the response.
Write ExceptionHandlingMiddleware mapping DomainException->400, NotFoundException->404, StudyLockedException->409, DbUpdateConcurrencyException->409, everything else->500.
Return ProblemDetails with type/title/status/detail plus the correlation id as an extension member.
Package both as an AddApiDefaults() extension the four Api projects call in one line.

tasks.title: Contracts project for integration events
tasks.details: One shared assembly of immutable event records. Versioned by adding fields, never by repurposing one.
acceptanceCriteria: Both the publisher and the consumer compile against the same record type
steps: Create MediView.Contracts as a classlib referenced by every Api and Infrastructure project.
Declare the three MVP events as records: ImagesImported, ReportFinalized, DoctorRegistered.
Write the rule at the top of the file: additive changes only.

sections.name: Local Infrastructure (Docker Compose)
sections.goal: Day 4 - One `docker compose up` gives you PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ and Seq. Services run from the IDE against them. No Aspire, no Kubernetes - that is deferred scope.

tasks.title: docker-compose.yml with the four dependencies
tasks.details: Postgres 16, Redis 7, RabbitMQ with the management UI, Seq for log viewing. Named volumes so data survives a restart.
acceptanceCriteria: `docker compose up -d --wait` returns healthy for all four
RabbitMQ management UI reachable on :15672, Seq on :5341
steps: Write docker-compose.yml with the four services, fixed host ports and named volumes.
Add healthchecks to each so `docker compose up --wait` blocks until they are actually ready.
Create one database per service (mediview_identity, mediview_studies, ...) via an init SQL script mounted into the postgres container.

tasks.title: Connection strings and user-secrets
tasks.details: Local secrets never touch the repo. Typed options validated at boot so a bad value fails at startup, not at 2 a.m.
acceptanceCriteria: Cloning the repo and running the app fails with a clear message about the missing secret, not a null reference
steps: Add appsettings.Development.json with non-secret defaults (hosts, ports, database names).
Run `dotnet user-secrets init` in each Api project and store passwords there.
Bind a typed options class per concern and call .ValidateDataAnnotations().ValidateOnStart().

tasks.title: Serilog to console and Seq
tasks.details: Structured JSON logs enriched with CorrelationId, UserId and ServiceName. Never log PHI - log ids.
acceptanceCriteria: A request produces one enriched log line visible in Seq
Searching Seq by correlation id shows the whole request
steps: Add Serilog with the Console and Seq sinks in a shared AddLogging extension.
Enrich with ServiceName from the assembly name plus the correlation id from the log scope.
Add UseSerilogRequestLogging() to the pipeline.
Write the rule in the README: no patient name, DOB or report text in any log statement.

tasks.title: Run scripts and health checks
tasks.details: Make the whole thing startable by someone who has never seen it - including you in three weeks.
acceptanceCriteria: A clean clone is running end to end in under 5 minutes
steps: Add /health/live and /health/ready (ready checks Postgres + Redis) to every Api.
Add a run.sh / run.ps1 that brings up compose then `dotnet run` the gateway and services.
Write the 6-line 'getting started' block in the README and follow it on a clean clone.

sections.name: Identity Service (auth + people)
sections.goal: Days 5-9 - One service that owns users, patients, doctors and doctor schedules. JWT with a single role claim and three policies. The v3 role/permission matrix (3 tables + an admin UI) is cut: a 3-role system does not need one to teach authorization.

tasks.title: Scaffold the four Identity projects and the DbContext
tasks.details: First service, so this is where you set the template every later service copies.
acceptanceCriteria: The service starts, connects to Postgres and answers /health/ready
steps: Create IdentityDbContext with HasDefaultSchema("identity") and UseSnakeCaseNamingConvention().
Add Npgsql with EnableRetryOnFailure(); turn lazy loading off.
Add AddInfrastructure(config) and AddApplication() extensions so Program.cs reads like a table of contents.

tasks.title: Model User, Patient, Doctor and DoctorSchedule
tasks.details: Four small aggregates. Users hold one role - the compaction that deletes roles, permissions, role_permissions and user_roles. Mrn is a value object with its own format rule.
acceptanceCriteria: Constructing a Doctor without a licence number throws DomainException
Mrn rejects a string that is not MRN-####
steps: Create User : AggregateRoot<Guid> with Email, PasswordHash, FullName, Role (enum), Dob, Gender, IsActive.
Create Patient with a Mrn value object, and Doctor with LicenseNumber, Specialty, Department.
Create DoctorSchedule (DayOfWeek, StartTime, EndTime, SlotMinutes) with the invariant EndTime > StartTime.
Put IUserRepository / IPatientRepository / IDoctorRepository in Domain, next to their aggregates.

tasks.title: EF configurations, schema and first migration
tasks.details: Map the five identity tables exactly as mediview-mvp.dbml specifies.
acceptanceCriteria: The identity schema has exactly 5 tables
Two patients registered concurrently get different MRNs
steps: Write one IEntityTypeConfiguration per aggregate; enums as strings via HasConversion<string>().
Own the Mrn value object with OwnsOne; add the unique indexes on email, mrn and license_number.
Create a Postgres sequence for MRN numbering and a helper that formats MRN-{seq:0000}.
Run `dotnet ef migrations add InitialIdentity -p ...Infrastructure -s ...Api` and apply it.

tasks.title: Patient self-registration
tasks.details: The only self-service signup. Creating the user and its Patient row with an MRN is one transaction.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /auth/register creates exactly one user and one patient row
A duplicate email returns 409 ProblemDetails, not a 500
steps: Add a password hasher (ASP.NET Core PasswordHasher or BCrypt) behind an IPasswordHasher port.
Write RegisterPatientCommand + handler: uniqueness check, hash, create User(role=patient) and Patient(mrn) together, save once.
Return a Failure result (not an exception) when the email is taken; map it to 409.
Add a validator for email format and password strength.

tasks.title: Login, JWT issuance and refresh-token rotation
tasks.details: Access token ~15 min carrying sub, email, role and (for doctors) doctor_id. Refresh tokens are hashed at rest, single-use and rotate on every exchange.
acceptanceCriteria: A refresh token used twice is rejected the second time
A doctor's JWT contains a doctor_id claim
steps: Write LoginCommand: verify the hash, issue a JWT with the role claim, issue a refresh token and store only its hash.
Write RefreshCommand: look up by hash, reject if revoked or expired, revoke the old row and issue a new pair.
Configure JwtBearer validation (issuer, audience, lifetime, signing key, ClockSkew 30s) in a shared AddJwtAuth extension the other services also call.
Add a Logout that revokes the refresh token.

tasks.title: Three authorization policies
tasks.details: PatientOnly / DoctorOnly / AdminOnly. The rule that matters: an admin is NOT a doctor - the admin policy must never satisfy a report-writing endpoint.
acceptanceCriteria: A patient token gets 403 on an admin endpoint
An admin token gets 403 on the report-write endpoint (verified later in P11)
steps: Add AddAuthorizationBuilder() policies over the role claim in a shared extension.
Apply .RequireAuthorization("AdminOnly") to the doctor-creation endpoint.
Write the note in the ADR: UI checks are convenience, the API is the authority.

tasks.title: Admin creates a doctor and their weekly schedule
tasks.details: One form, one command. The v3 credential upload plus verification workflow is deferred - the admin attests and that is recorded.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /admin/doctors creates a user and a doctor in one transaction
Setting a schedule twice does not duplicate rows
steps: Write CreateDoctorCommand: create User(role=doctor) with a temporary password + Doctor row in one transaction.
Write SetDoctorScheduleCommand taking a list of (dayOfWeek, start, end, slotMinutes); replace the set atomically.
Raise the DoctorRegistered domain event (published in P08).

tasks.title: Availability query - expand schedules into bookable slots
tasks.details: The one piece of real algorithm in this service: turn weekly rules into concrete slots for a date range.
acceptanceCriteria: A Mon-Fri 08:00-16:00 / 30-min doctor yields 16 slots per weekday and none on Sunday
Slots before now are excluded
steps: Write GetDoctorAvailabilityQuery(doctorId, fromDate, toDate).
Expand each DoctorSchedule row across the dates in range, stepping by SlotMinutes, skipping slots in the past.
Return slots as (start, end) UTC instants - the Studies service subtracts the booked ones.
Unit-test the expansion including a range that crosses a week boundary.

tasks.title: Endpoints, seed data and a .http smoke file
tasks.details: A seeded database you can demo from on day one, and a request file that proves every endpoint.
acceptanceCriteria: Running the .http file top to bottom passes every request
A fresh database is demo-ready after one startup
steps: Write AuthEndpoints and AdminEndpoints as Minimal API groups, one file per aggregate.
Seed on startup (dev only): 1 admin, 2 doctors with schedules, 3 patients with MRNs.
Add identity.http covering register -> login -> refresh -> create doctor -> availability.
Add a lookup endpoint GET /internal/people/{id} returning name + mrn - the Studies service calls this to take its snapshot.

sections.name: Studies Service - the DDD core
sections.goal: Days 10-16 - The richest aggregate in the system and the single source of truth for the workflow. Booking was folded in from its own microservice: an appointment exists only to produce a Study, so they share a transaction boundary. Spend your best week here - this is the section that teaches DDD.

tasks.title: Scaffold the Studies service from the Identity template
tasks.details: Same four projects, same DbContext conventions, schema "studies".
acceptanceCriteria: The service starts and a doctor JWT issued by Identity is accepted here
steps: Copy the project structure and the AddInfrastructure/AddApplication shape from Identity.
Create StudiesDbContext with HasDefaultSchema("studies").
Register AddApiDefaults() and AddJwtAuth() so auth works from the first endpoint.

tasks.title: Study aggregate root and its status state machine
tasks.details: Four statuses, and the transitions are the business rules. Every illegal move throws before it reaches the database - that is what makes this a domain model rather than a data model.
acceptanceCriteria: Calling Complete() on a todo study throws, and no row changes
StartRead on a study with no images throws with a message the UI can show
steps: Create Study : AggregateRoot<Guid> with a private constructor and a static Study.Schedule(...) factory.
Implement StartRead(doctorId), RequestReDiagnosis(reason), Complete(), and AdminOverride(to, actor, reason).
Encode the legal transitions in one place: todo->in_progress, in_progress->done, in_progress->re_diagnosis, re_diagnosis->in_progress. Everything else throws InvalidStatusTransitionException.
Enforce the acquisition guard: StartRead throws if ImagesImportedAt is null.
Raise a domain event on every successful transition.

tasks.title: StudyStatusHistory as an owned child collection
tasks.details: The entity that proves the aggregate boundary is real: nothing outside Study may insert a history row.
acceptanceCriteria: Every status change writes exactly one history row in the same SaveChanges
AdminOverride without a reason throws
steps: Add a private List<StudyStatusHistory> exposed as IReadOnlyCollection<StudyStatusHistory>.
Append a history row inside the transition method itself - never from a handler.
Record from, to, changedBy, changedByRole and reason; make reason mandatory for AdminOverride.
Confirm there is no IStudyStatusHistoryRepository anywhere - if you wanted one, the boundary is wrong.

tasks.title: Appointment entity and the no-double-booking invariant
tasks.details: Defence in depth: check in the handler for a friendly error, and a unique index in the database because two requests can pass the check at the same time.
acceptanceCriteria: Two concurrent bookings of one slot produce one appointment and one 409
steps: Create Appointment with PatientId, DoctorId, ScheduledStart/End, Status and Reason.
In the booking handler, query for an existing booked appointment at that slot and return a Failure result if found.
Add the unique index (doctor_id, scheduled_start) and catch the Postgres 23505 to map it to the same 409.
Write the test that fires two identical bookings in parallel and asserts exactly one succeeds.

tasks.title: EF configurations, snake_case mapping and optimistic concurrency
tasks.details: Map the five studies tables. Concurrency via Postgres xmin so a lost update surfaces as a 409 instead of silently overwriting a colleague.
acceptanceCriteria: The studies schema has exactly 5 tables and matches the DBML
A stale update throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException and the middleware returns 409
steps: Write StudyConfiguration, AppointmentConfiguration, StudyStatusHistoryConfiguration, StudyLockConfiguration, AuditLogConfiguration.
Enums as strings; jsonb for audit before/after; the composite worklist index (status, priority, study_date).
Add `b.Property<uint>("xmin").IsRowVersion().HasColumnName("xmin")` on Study.
Configure History with WithOne().OnDelete(Cascade) and access through the backing field.
Run the InitialStudies migration and verify against mediview-mvp.dbml.

tasks.title: Repositories and the unit-of-work rule
tasks.details: Repository interfaces live in Domain with their aggregate; implementations in Infrastructure. SaveChangesAsync IS the unit of work - do not wrap DbContext in an IUnitOfWork that only forwards.
acceptanceCriteria: A handler loads an aggregate, mutates it and calls SaveChangesAsync once
No repository returns IQueryable
steps: Define IStudyRepository (GetByIdAsync with Include(History), Add) and IAppointmentRepository in Domain.
Implement them over StudiesDbContext; never expose IQueryable from a repository.
Add a DomainEventDispatcher hooked to SaveChangesAsync that collects and clears events after a successful save.
Write the rule in the ADR so you do not re-litigate it in week 4.

tasks.title: BookAppointment: the snapshot pattern in action
tasks.details: The command that replaces the whole v3 cross-service query stack. One typed HttpClient call to Identity at booking time copies mrn, patient name and doctor name onto the Study - after that the worklist never leaves this database.
acceptanceCriteria: Booking creates one appointment and one Study in one transaction
The Study row carries patient_mrn, patient_name and doctor_name
Identity being down returns a clean 503, not a 500
steps: Add a typed IIdentityApi HttpClient with a Polly retry + circuit breaker, pointed at Identity's /internal/people endpoint.

Write BookAppointmentCommand: fetch patient + doctor details, verify the slot against the availability the client returns, create Appointment, then create Study in status todo with the snapshot columns filled.
Generate StudyNumber (STU-###) from a Postgres sequence and a StudyInstanceUid (a DICOM-shaped UID with your own root).
Return the study id so the UI can navigate straight to it.
Write the comment explaining WHY the snapshot is correct: DICOM embeds PatientName at acquisition; a later rename must not rewrite history.

tasks.title: The doctor worklist query
tasks.details: The hot path. AsNoTracking + Select into a flat DTO, sorted stat-first, cursor- or offset-paged. No Dapper in the MVP - projection over a single local table is already one round trip.
acceptanceCriteria: The worklist returns in one SQL round trip
EXPLAIN shows an index scan, not a sequential scan, on 10k seeded rows
steps: Write GetWorklistQuery(doctorId?, statuses[], search, skip, take).
Project directly into WorklistItemDto - never return an entity from a query handler.
Left-join the active lock row so each item carries lockedBy (null when free).
Order by priority desc then study_date; verify the composite index is used with EXPLAIN.
Add the rule to your notes: never .ToList().Skip() and never a query inside a foreach.

tasks.title: Study detail and patient timeline queries
tasks.details: What screen 3 and screen 5 read.
acceptanceCriteria: A patient can only fetch their own studies - enforced in the handler from the JWT sub, not from a route parameter
steps: Write GetStudyByIdQuery returning the study plus its ordered status history.
Write GetMyStudiesQuery(patientId) for the patient portal.
Both AsNoTracking with explicit projection.

tasks.title: MarkImagesImported
tasks.details: The guard that stops a doctor reading an empty study. Called by an endpoint now; rewired to the ImagesImported event in P08.
acceptanceCriteria: Importing images sets images_imported_at and leaves the status at todo
Calling it twice is harmless
steps: Add Study.MarkImagesImported(at) - idempotent, and it must NOT change the status.
Expose POST /internal/studies/{id}/images-imported for now.
Assert in a test that a todo study stays todo after import.

tasks.title: Admin status override with a mandatory reason
tasks.details: Break-glass. An admin can move a study anywhere, but never without a reason and never silently.
acceptanceCriteria: An override without a reason returns 400
One override produces one history row and one audit row
steps: Write OverrideStudyStatusCommand guarded by AdminOnly, requiring a non-empty reason.
Call Study.AdminOverride(...) so the history row is written by the aggregate.
Write an audit_log row with action study.status.override, before/after as jsonb, in the same transaction.
Reject an override that an ordinary transition would allow anyway - it should go through the normal path.

tasks.title: Unit tests for the state machine
tasks.details: The highest value-per-line tests in the whole project, and they need no database.
acceptanceCriteria: The Study aggregate has >90% line coverage from tests that run in under a second
steps: Write a table-driven test over all 16 (from,to) pairs asserting legal moves succeed and illegal ones throw.
Test the images-imported guard, the mandatory override reason, and that every transition appends exactly one history row.
Keep them pure - constructing a Study must not need EF, Postgres or a mock.

sections.name: Imaging Service (DICOM)
sections.goal: Days 17-21 - Accept .dcm uploads, parse them with fo-dicom, keep pixels in blob storage and metadata in Postgres, and serve the bytes back over a WADO-shaped endpoint that Cornerstone can consume. Two tables. The v3 import_jobs queue and saved annotations are deferred.

tasks.title: Scaffold the Imaging service and model Series/Instance
tasks.details: Series is the aggregate root; Instance is its child. The Study lives in another service, so study_id here is just a uuid.
acceptanceCriteria: The imaging schema has exactly 2 tables
Adding an instance through the aggregate keeps instance_count correct
steps: Create the four projects and ImagingDbContext with schema "imaging".
Model Series : AggregateRoot with a private List<Instance> and AddInstance(...) maintaining InstanceCount.
Write the two EF configurations with unique indexes on series_instance_uid and sop_instance_uid.
Run the InitialImaging migration.

tasks.title: IBlobStore port with a local-disk adapter
tasks.details: The interface lives in Application, the adapter in Infrastructure. Local disk in dev; Azure Blob is a same-shape adapter you can add in an hour if you ever want it.
acceptanceCriteria: The upload path never mentions the file system outside the adapter
steps: Define IBlobStore { PutAsync(key, stream), OpenReadAsync(key), DeleteAsync(key) } in Application/Ports.
Implement LocalDiskBlobStore writing under a configured root, keyed studies/{studyUid}/{seriesUid}/{sopUid}.dcm.
Register it by configuration so swapping the adapter is a one-line change.
Add the folder to .gitignore.

tasks.title: Parse uploaded DICOM with fo-dicom
tasks.details: Read the tags the viewport actually needs and reject anything that is not a DICOM file.
acceptanceCriteria: A non-DICOM file returns 400 with a clear message
A real chest x-ray uploads and its rows/columns match the file
steps: Add the fo-dicom package and open the uploaded stream with DicomFile.OpenAsync.
Extract StudyInstanceUID (0020,000D), SeriesInstanceUID (0020,000E), SOPInstanceUID (0008,0018), InstanceNumber, Rows, Columns, WindowCenter, WindowWidth, Modality, BodyPartExamined.
Validate the file has the DICM preamble and reject with 400 otherwise; cap the upload size.
Handle a missing window center/width by leaving them null - the viewer falls back to a computed default.

tasks.title: Upload endpoint - the admin x-ray simulation
tasks.details: Multi-file upload for one study. Pixels to the blob store, metadata to Postgres, in that order, and cleaned up if the save fails.
acceptanceCriteria: Uploading 12 files of one series creates 1 series row and 12 instance rows
A mid-way failure leaves no orphaned blobs
steps: Write ImportInstancesCommand(studyId, IFormFileCollection) behind AdminOnly.
For each file: parse, write the blob, then add the Instance to its Series (create the Series on first sight of its UID).
SaveChanges once at the end; if it throws, delete the blobs you just wrote.
Return a summary (series created, instances added, total bytes) for the admin screen.

tasks.title: Publish ImagesImported
tasks.details: The fact that unblocks the read. Raised here, consumed by Studies in P08; until then call the internal endpoint directly.
acceptanceCriteria: After an import the Study shows images_imported_at set
steps: Raise an ImagesImported(studyId, seriesCount, instanceCount, importedAtUtc) domain event on a successful import.
For now, translate it in a handler that calls the Studies internal endpoint over a typed client.
Leave a TODO pointing at P08 where this becomes an outbox publish.

tasks.title: QIDO-shaped metadata endpoints
tasks.details: Just enough DICOMweb shape for the viewer to discover what to load.
acceptanceCriteria: The viewer can build a full image stack from these two calls
steps: GET /studies/{studyId}/series -> series list with instance counts.
GET /series/{seriesId}/instances -> ordered instance metadata including window center/width.
Project into DTOs; order by instance_number so the stack scrolls in the right order.

tasks.title: WADO-shaped retrieve endpoint
tasks.details: Stream the original bytes back. No re-encoding, no buffering the whole file in memory.
acceptanceCriteria: Cornerstone loads an image straight from this URL
A 40 MB CT slice streams without the process memory spiking
steps: GET /instances/{sopInstanceUid} returning application/dicom from IBlobStore.OpenReadAsync.
Use Results.Stream / a FileStreamResult so a large file never lands fully in memory.
Set ETag/Cache-Control - instances are immutable, so they cache forever.
Require an authenticated caller; note in the ADR that a real deployment would also check the study is assigned to this doctor.

tasks.title: Sample data set and an imaging smoke test
tasks.details: You need real pixels to demo. Get them once and script the import.
acceptanceCriteria: `./seed-images.sh` imports a demo study end to end
steps: Download a small public de-identified DICOM set (e.g. a chest x-ray series) into test-data/, git-ignored.
Write imaging.http covering upload -> series -> instances -> retrieve.
Add an integration test with Testcontainers that imports two files and asserts the row counts.

sections.name: Single-Writer Lock (Redis) + SignalR
sections.goal: Days 22-25 - The feature that makes this project worth showing. One doctor edits a study at a time, enforced by a Redis lock with an owner token and a TTL, mirrored into Postgres for the UI and the audit trail, announced over SignalR. Cut from v3: lock_watchers and the notify-me-when-free flow.

tasks.title: Define the IStudyLockService port
tasks.details: The Application layer must never know Redis exists. Get the interface right and the rest is an adapter.
acceptanceCriteria: Handlers compile and test against the interface with no Redis reference
steps: Define IStudyLockService in Application/Ports: TryAcquire(studyId, doctorId, ttl) -> LockResult, Renew(studyId, ownerToken), Release(studyId, ownerToken, reason), GetOwner(studyId).
Make LockResult carry Acquired plus the current owner's id and name when it fails - the 409 body needs both.
Write an in-memory implementation first so you can unit-test the handlers with no Redis.

tasks.title: Redis lock adapter: SET NX PX with an owner token
tasks.details: The classic mistake is releasing someone else's lock after your TTL expired. The owner token plus a Lua compare-and-delete is what prevents it.
acceptanceCriteria: A release with the wrong token is a no-op
An expired lock is acquirable by another doctor with no manual cleanup
steps: Add StackExchange.Redis and register IConnectionMultiplexer as a singleton.
Acquire with `SET study-lock:{id} {ownerToken} NX PX {ttlMs}` where ownerToken is a fresh Guid.
Release with a Lua script that deletes only if the stored value equals the token; same idea for renew with PEXPIRE.
Return the existing owner on failure by reading a companion hash holding doctorId + doctorName.
Write down why RedLock across multiple masters is NOT needed here: one Redis instance, and the Postgres unique index is the backstop.

tasks.title: Acquire on open: the todo -> in_progress transition
tasks.details: Opening the viewport is the business event. Lock first, then transition, then mirror - and undo the lock if the transition throws.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening a study moves it to in_progress and writes a study_locks row
Opening a study with no images leaves no lock behind
steps: Write StartReadCommand(studyId): TryAcquire, then Study.StartRead(doctorId), then upsert the study_locks row, then SaveChanges.
If StartRead throws (no images, wrong status), release the Redis lock before letting the exception propagate.
Store the owner token in the response so the client sends it on heartbeat and release.
Make it idempotent: the same doctor re-opening their own locked study succeeds and returns the same token.

tasks.title: Heartbeat and TTL renewal
tasks.details: The client pings while the doctor is actually working. Only the owner may renew.
acceptanceCriteria: Closing the browser frees the study within the TTL with no server action
A heartbeat from another doctor is rejected
steps: Add POST /studies/{id}/lock/heartbeat taking the owner token; renew the Redis TTL and update last_heartbeat.
Ping every 30 s from the client with a 15-minute TTL - a browser crash frees the study automatically.
Reject a heartbeat from a non-owner with 409, and have the client treat that as 'you lost the lock' and go read-only.

tasks.title: Release paths and the expiry sweeper
tasks.details: Three ways a lock ends normally, plus a background job that reconciles the Postgres mirror with reality.
acceptanceCriteria: An expired lock is reconciled in Postgres within a minute
The background service does not throw on an empty result set
steps: Release on explicit close (reason manual), on report finalize (P07), and on TTL expiry.
Write a BackgroundService that every minute finds study_locks rows with released_at null and expires_at in the past, marks them ttl_expired, and pushes LockReleased.
Use IServiceScopeFactory inside the background service - never inject a scoped DbContext into a singleton.
Decide and document what happens to the study status when a lock expires mid-read: it STAYS in_progress (the read is unfinished, not abandoned).

tasks.title: StudyLockedException -> 409 with the owner in the body
tasks.details: Every write to a locked study fails the same way, and the message tells the second doctor who to go talk to.
acceptanceCriteria: A second doctor's write returns 409 naming the owner and the elapsed time
The check is server-side - bypassing the UI still gets 409
steps: Create StudyLockedException carrying ownerName and acquiredAt.
Map it in the shared exception middleware to 409 ProblemDetails with ownerName, ownerId and elapsedMinutes as extensions.
Guard every mutating study and report endpoint with an ownership check, not just the UI.

tasks.title: SignalR StudyHub
tasks.details: Announcements only. The hub is never the source of truth - Redis is. A dropped socket must never grant or extend a lock.
acceptanceCriteria: Two browsers on the same study see the lock change within a second
The hub never mutates state
steps: Add StudyHub with [Authorize]; join `study:{studyId}` and `worklist` groups, never address connection ids.
Publish LockAcquired, LockReleased and StatusChanged after the transaction commits, not inside it.
Wire JWT over the access_token query string for the WebSocket handshake (OnMessageReceived).
Skip the Redis backplane for the MVP and write the one-line note: it is required the moment you run two instances.

tasks.title: The concurrency test that proves it
tasks.details: The demo moment. Automate it so you trust it, then perform it live with two browser windows.
acceptanceCriteria: 10 parallel acquires yield exactly one winner, repeatably
The two-window demo works without a page refresh
steps: Write an integration test firing 10 parallel StartRead calls for one study and asserting exactly 1 succeeds and 9 return 409.
Assert the 9 failures all name the same owner.
Write the manual demo script: two windows, two doctors, open, watch the second go read-only, finalize, watch it unlock.

sections.name: Reporting Service (report + medications)
sections.goal: Days 26-30 - The read itself. A Report aggregate with an owned medication collection - one child table that replaces the entire v3 Prescription microservice. Finalizing is the transaction that closes the study, and a re-diagnosis creates a second report rather than editing the first.

tasks.title: Scaffold Reporting and model the Report aggregate
tasks.details: Second aggregate-heavy service, so it should feel routine by now. That familiarity is the point of a consistent template.
acceptanceCriteria: The reporting schema has exactly 3 tables
steps: Create the four projects and ReportingDbContext with schema "reporting".
Model Report : AggregateRoot with StudyId, DoctorId, DoctorName, ReportNumber, Status, Findings, Impression, Decision, FinalizedAt.
Add a private List<ReportMedication> exposed read-only, with AddMedication / RemoveMedication.
Model the Drug lookup entity.

tasks.title: Finalize invariants - the rules that make a report clinical
tasks.details: A draft is freely editable; a finalized report is frozen forever. Getting this right is the difference between a CRUD app and a medical record.
acceptanceCriteria: Finalizing without an impression throws
Editing a finalized report throws at the domain level, not in the endpoint
steps: Implement Finalize(decision): throw unless Findings and Impression are non-empty and Status is draft.
Throw on ANY mutation once Status is finalized - including AddMedication.
Stamp FinalizedAt from an injected IClock, never DateTime.Now.
Raise ReportFinalized(studyId, reportId, decision) as a domain event.
Write the ADR note: a correction is a NEW report row, which is why study_id is not unique.

tasks.title: EF configuration, drug seed and migration
tasks.details: Map three tables and seed the formulary the composer types against.
acceptanceCriteria: The drug type-ahead returns results on a fresh database
Two reports created concurrently get different numbers
steps: Write the three IEntityTypeConfigurations; medications cascade-delete with their report.
Seed ~30 common drugs (code, name, form, strength) from a JSON file at startup in dev.
Create a sequence for ReportNumber formatted RP-####.
Run the InitialReporting migration.

tasks.title: Create draft and save draft - lock ownership enforced
tasks.details: Only the doctor holding the study lock may write. Reporting does not own the lock, so it asks Studies.
acceptanceCriteria: A doctor who does not hold the lock cannot create or edit a report
An admin token is refused here too - admins do not diagnose
steps: Add a typed IStudiesApi client with an endpoint GET /internal/studies/{id}/lock returning the current owner.
Write CreateDraftCommand: verify the caller owns the lock, verify the study is in_progress, create the report.
Write SaveDraftCommand for findings/impression with the same ownership check.
Return 409 StudyLocked when the caller is not the owner - the same shape as P06-T06.
Autosave the draft from the UI every 20 s so a lost lock never costs the doctor their typing.

tasks.title: Medication composer commands
tasks.details: What used to be a whole service is now two commands on an aggregate.
acceptanceCriteria: Medications can be added and removed on a draft and not on a finalized report
Deactivating a drug in the catalog does not alter an existing report - the name is snapshotted
steps: Write AddMedicationCommand(reportId, drugId?, drugName, dosage, frequency, duration, quantity) - snapshot drugName at add time.
Write RemoveMedicationCommand; both go through the aggregate, both refuse once finalized.
Write GetDrugsQuery(search) for the type-ahead, AsNoTracking, top 20.
Allow a free-text medication (drugId null) so the formulary never blocks a doctor.

tasks.title: Finalize: one transaction, three effects
tasks.details: Stamp the report, write the outbox row, release the lock. All or nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: Finalizing writes exactly one outbox row in the same transaction as the report update
The study unlocks and the second doctor's viewport goes live within a second
steps: Write FinalizeReportCommand: ownership check, Report.Finalize(decision), save.
In the same SaveChanges write the ReportFinalized outbox row (wired properly in P08).
After the commit, call Studies to release the lock with reason manual.
Handle the awkward case explicitly: if the lock was already lost, the finalize still succeeds - the doctor's work is not thrown away.

tasks.title: PDF export with QuestPDF
tasks.details: The patient-facing artefact: header, patient and study identifiers, findings, impression, medications, doctor and finalize timestamp.
acceptanceCriteria: A finalized report downloads as a readable one-page PDF
A draft PDF is clearly watermarked
steps: Add QuestPDF (community licence) and write one ReportDocument class.
Generate on demand from GET /reports/{id}/pdf rather than storing a file - regeneration is cheap and there is no blob to keep in sync.
Include the report number, study number and MRN in the header; mark drafts with a DRAFT watermark.
Return 403 unless the caller is the reporting doctor, an admin, or the patient the study belongs to.

tasks.title: Report queries for both portals
tasks.details: The doctor needs their drafts; the patient needs their finalized results.
acceptanceCriteria: A patient cannot fetch a draft report by guessing its id
A re-diagnosed study shows two reports in order
steps: Write GetReportByStudyQuery returning the latest report plus medications.
Write GetMyReportsQuery(patientId) filtered to finalized only - a patient never sees a draft.
Write GetReportHistoryQuery(studyId) returning all reports oldest-first, which is how a re-diagnosis chain reads.

tasks.title: Unit tests for the Report aggregate
tasks.details: Same discipline as P04-T12: no database, sub-second, and they encode the clinical rules.
acceptanceCriteria: The Report aggregate has >90% line coverage
steps: Test finalize with missing findings, missing impression, wrong status, and the happy path.
Test that every mutation after finalize throws.
Test that the medication collection cannot be mutated through the exposed IReadOnlyCollection.

sections.name: Integration Events (MassTransit + Outbox)
sections.goal: Days 31-32 - Replace the temporary direct HTTP calls with real async choreography. Three events, two consumers, one transactional outbox. This is the microservice lesson: services react to facts, they do not command each other.

tasks.title: Wire MassTransit over RabbitMQ in all four services
tasks.details: One shared AddMessaging(config) extension so every service is configured identically.
acceptanceCriteria: All four services connect and declare their endpoints on startup
steps: Add MassTransit.RabbitMQ; configure the host from options, kebab-case endpoint naming, and consumer registration by assembly scan.
Set a retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, 5 attempts, then the error queue.
Verify the queues and exchanges appear in the RabbitMQ management UI on first start.

tasks.title: Transactional outbox
tasks.details: Without it, a crash between SaveChanges and Publish silently loses the event and the study never closes. This is the single most important reliability lesson in the project.
acceptanceCriteria: The outbox tables exist and drain
A process kill after commit still delivers the event
steps: Enable the MassTransit EF Core outbox on Imaging and Reporting (AddEntityFrameworkOutbox with UsePostgres + UseBusOutbox).
Add the outbox migration to both services.
Replace every direct IPublishEndpoint call inside a handler with a publish that enlists in the ambient transaction.
Prove it: pause the process between commit and delivery (a debugger breakpoint is enough), kill it, and confirm the event is still delivered on restart.

tasks.title: Publish the three integration events
tasks.details: Translate domain events into contract records at the edge of the service - domain events never leave their service.
acceptanceCriteria: No integration event carries a domain entity
Each event is published exactly once per business action
steps: Imaging publishes ImagesImported after a successful import (replacing the P05-T05 HTTP call).
Reporting publishes ReportFinalized inside the finalize transaction.
Identity publishes DoctorRegistered when an admin creates a doctor.
Keep the contract records in MediView.Contracts and never reference a domain type from them.

tasks.title: Consumers in the Studies service
tasks.details: Studies reacts to both facts. This is where the workflow actually becomes distributed.
acceptanceCriteria: Finalizing a report closes the study with no synchronous call between the two services
The patient's status page updates without a refresh
steps: ImagesImportedConsumer -> Study.MarkImagesImported; the status must stay todo.
ReportFinalizedConsumer -> Study.Complete() or Study.RequestReDiagnosis() based on the decision, then release the lock.
Push StatusChanged over SignalR from the consumer so the patient's page updates live.
Delete the temporary internal HTTP endpoints the consumers replace, or mark them internal-only for tests.

tasks.title: Idempotent consumers, DLQ and an end-to-end message test
tasks.details: At-least-once delivery is guaranteed; exactly-once is not. Your consumers must be able to see the same message twice.
acceptanceCriteria: Delivering the same event twice changes nothing the second time
A poison message lands in the error queue instead of looping
steps: Make both consumers idempotent - MarkImagesImported already is; make the status transitions a no-op if the study is already in the target state.
Configure the error/dead-letter queue and look at it deliberately once so you know where it is.
Write an integration test with the MassTransit in-memory harness: publish ReportFinalized twice, assert one status change.
Log every consumed message with its MessageId and correlation id.

sections.name: API Gateway (YARP)
sections.goal: Day 33 - One ingress in front of four services so the Blazor app talks to a single origin. Deliberately thin: routing, JWT, CORS, rate limiting, aggregated health. No BFF aggregation, no request transformation.

tasks.title: YARP project with route and cluster configuration
tasks.details: Config-driven, not code-driven, so adding a service is an appsettings edit.
acceptanceCriteria: Every service is reachable through the gateway
The SignalR connection upgrades to WebSockets through the gateway
steps: Create MediView.Gateway, add Yarp.ReverseProxy and LoadFromConfig.
Define four clusters and path-prefix routes: /api/identity/**, /api/studies/**, /api/imaging/**, /api/reporting/**.
Strip the prefix with a PathRemovePrefix transform so the services stay unaware of the gateway.
Proxy the SignalR hub path with WebSockets enabled - this is the one that always gets forgotten.

tasks.title: JWT validation at the edge
tasks.details: Validate once at the gateway and again in each service - defence in depth, and the services stay independently callable in tests.
acceptanceCriteria: An anonymous call to a protected route is rejected at the gateway with 401
A service called directly still enforces its own auth
steps: Call the shared AddJwtAuth extension in the gateway.
Require authorization on all routes except /api/identity/auth/**.
Forward the original Authorization header untouched to the downstream service.

tasks.title: CORS, rate limiting and correlation-id propagation
tasks.details: The cross-cutting policies that belong at the edge and nowhere else.
acceptanceCriteria: A brute-force login attempt is throttled at the gateway
One correlation id appears in the logs of every service involved in a request
steps: Add a named CORS policy allowing the Blazor origin with credentials.
Add the built-in rate limiter: a fixed window per authenticated user, and a tighter one on the auth endpoints.
Ensure X-Correlation-Id is created at the gateway if absent and forwarded, so one trace spans gateway -> service -> bus.

tasks.title: Aggregated health and API docs
tasks.details: One URL that tells you whether the system is up.
acceptanceCriteria: /health shows all four services green after `docker compose up` + run
steps: Add a /health endpoint that fans out to the four /health/ready endpoints and reports each.
Expose OpenAPI/Scalar per service behind the gateway for manual testing.
Add the gateway to the run script and README.

sections.name: Blazor Web - 8 pages + DICOM viewport
sections.goal: Days 34-41 - Blazor Server, 8 pages instead of the 15 mocked screens. Cut: wallet, cart & checkout, follow-up booking, the roles/permissions matrix and the mobile layout. Build a throwaway page as you finish each service earlier in the plan; this block is where they become real.

tasks.title: App shell, auth state and typed API clients
tasks.details: Get the plumbing right once so eight pages are eight pages of markup, not eight pages of plumbing.
acceptanceCriteria: Signing in switches the nav to the right role
A 401 from the API refreshes the token once and retries, then redirects to login
steps: Create MediView.Web as a Blazor Web App with the InteractiveServer render mode.
Store the JWT in a protected browser-storage session and implement a custom AuthenticationStateProvider over it.
Register one typed HttpClient per service pointed at the gateway, with a delegating handler that attaches the bearer token and a Polly retry + circuit breaker.
Add CascadingAuthenticationState and a role-aware nav shell (patient / doctor / admin).
Structure by feature: Features/Auth, Features/Booking, Features/Studies, Features/Viewport, Features/Admin.

tasks.title: Page 1 - sign in and register
tasks.details: Screen 01 of the mockups. Register creates a patient only; doctor and admin accounts are provisioned internally.
acceptanceCriteria: A new patient can register and land on their empty studies page
A wrong password shows a message, not a stack trace
steps: Build the split panel from the mockup: product pitch left, form right.
Two tabs: sign in, and register with email, full name, password, DOB and gender.
Show server validation errors from the ProblemDetails body, field by field.
Redirect by role after login: patient -> /my-studies, doctor -> /worklist, admin -> /admin/import.

tasks.title: Page 2 - patient books a checkup
tasks.details: Screen 02. Three steps: pick a doctor, pick a slot inside their working hours, confirm.
acceptanceCriteria: A patient can book only inside the doctor's schedule
Booking creates a study visible immediately on the studies page
steps: Step 1: list doctors with specialty and department from Identity.
Step 2: call availability for the next 14 days and render a day/slot grid with taken slots disabled.
Step 3: confirmation panel with the doctor, slot and reason-for-visit textarea; POST the booking.
On success navigate to the created study and show the To do badge.
Handle the 409 double-booking race by refreshing the slot grid and telling the user plainly.

tasks.title: Page 3 - patient studies, status timeline and result
tasks.details: Screens 03 merged into one page: the list, the status timeline, the finalized report, its medications and the PDF link. The cart, wallet and bill panels from the mockup are cut.
acceptanceCriteria: The status badge changes live when the doctor finalizes
A draft report is never visible to the patient
steps: List the patient's studies with the four status badges using the exact labels: To do, In progress, Re-diagnosis, Done.
Render the status timeline from study_status_history.
When a finalized report exists, show findings, impression, decision, the medication table and a Download PDF button.
Subscribe to SignalR StatusChanged for the open study so the badge moves without a refresh.
Show the images as a count and an Imported-at timestamp, not a viewer - patients do not read their own x-rays.

tasks.title: Page 4 - doctor worklist
tasks.details: Screen 05. The doctor's home. Sorting is clinical: stat, then urgent, then routine, then by date.
acceptanceCriteria: The worklist updates live as another doctor opens and closes studies
Sorting puts stat studies first
steps: Table with study number, patient MRN and name, modality, body part, priority, status and lock owner.
Filter chips by status and a text search; Virtualize the rows.
Show a lock chip with the owner's name on studies someone else is reading.
Subscribe to the worklist SignalR group for StudyImported / LockAcquired / LockReleased / StatusChanged.
Disable Open with a tooltip when images_imported_at is null - fail in the UI before the API has to.

tasks.title: Cornerstone.js interop module
tasks.details: The fiddliest part of the project. Do it as its own task, with a hello-world image, before wiring it to real data.
acceptanceCriteria: A DICOM image renders in the browser from the imaging service
Navigating away and back does not leak a second viewport instance
steps: Add cornerstone-core / cornerstone-wado-image-loader (or Cornerstone3D) via a static wwwroot bundle - no CDN.
Write viewport.js exporting init(element, config), loadStack(imageIds), setWindowLevel(c, w), reset(), dispose().
Load it from C# as an IJSObjectReference and dispose it in IAsyncDisposable - never leak listeners between studies.
Configure the WADO image loader to send the Authorization header to the imaging endpoint.
Render one hard-coded local .dcm before touching the API.

tasks.title: Page 5 - the DICOM viewport
tasks.details: Screen 06, the dark reading view. Everything a first-pass read actually needs and nothing more.
acceptanceCriteria: A doctor can window, zoom, pan and scroll a series smoothly
Switching series does not reload the page
steps: Two-column layout: series thumbnails left, viewport centre, study metadata right.
Build the image stack from the QIDO endpoints and hand the ids to loadStack.
Tools: window/level drag, zoom, pan, stack scroll, invert, reset - keyboard shortcuts for each.
Show the default window centre/width from the instance metadata, and the current values live.
Set ShouldRender to false while the canvas is being manipulated, and @key the series list.

tasks.title: Lock banner, heartbeat and the read-only state
tasks.details: Screens 06 and 07 are the same page in two states. This is the interaction the whole project is built around.
acceptanceCriteria: The second doctor sees a read-only viewport naming the owner
Closing the tab releases the study within the TTL
steps: On open, call StartRead; on success show a green YOU HOLD THE LOCK banner with an elapsed timer.
Start a 30-second heartbeat timer; stop it on dispose and on navigation.
On 409, render the amber LOCKED BY <name> banner, keep the viewport fully interactive for viewing and disable every write.
Warn at 2 minutes before the TTL expires and offer Keep reading, which forces a renew.
Release the lock on navigate-away, on logout and on component dispose.

tasks.title: Report editor and medication composer panel
tasks.details: Screens 11 and part of 06, merged into a side panel of the viewport instead of a separate screen.
acceptanceCriteria: A report can be written, medications added and the study finalized without leaving the viewport
Autosave survives a lost lock - the text is still there
steps: Slide-over panel with Findings and Impression textareas, autosaving every 20 s and on blur.
Medication rows with a drug type-ahead, dosage, frequency, duration, quantity and a remove button.
Finalize dialog forcing an explicit decision: Done (no further read) or Re-diagnosis (another read needed).
Block Finalize until findings and impression are non-empty - the same rule the aggregate enforces.
After finalize, show the confirmation, release the lock and navigate back to the worklist.

tasks.title: SignalR client as a single scoped service
tasks.details: One connection serves the whole shell. A connection per component is the mistake that makes Blazor feel broken.
acceptanceCriteria: One WebSocket connection per browser tab regardless of page
A server restart reconnects the client without a manual refresh
steps: Wrap HubConnection in a scoped RealtimeService started once at shell level.
Expose C# events components subscribe to, and unsubscribe in Dispose.
Handle reconnect with a backoff, and re-join groups after a reconnect.
Show a small connection-state indicator in the header so you can see disconnects during the demo.

tasks.title: Page 6 - admin doctor onboarding
tasks.details: Screen 08, simplified. One form; the credential upload and verification queue are deferred.
acceptanceCriteria: An admin can create a doctor who can then sign in and appear as bookable
steps: Table of doctors with name, licence number, specialty and department.
Create-doctor form: email, full name, licence, specialty, department, temporary password.
Weekly schedule editor: a row per day with start, end and slot minutes.
Show the generated credentials once, with a copy button.

tasks.title: Page 7 - admin x-ray import simulation
tasks.details: Screen 09. This stands in for the modality: pick a study, drop .dcm files, watch them attach.
acceptanceCriteria: Dropping a folder of a dozen slices attaches them to the study
The doctor's Open button becomes enabled without a page refresh
steps: Study picker filtered to studies with no images.
Multi-file drop zone accepting .dcm with a per-file progress list.
POST to the imaging upload endpoint and show the summary: series created, instances added, total bytes.
After success, show that the study now has images and is ready to read.

tasks.title: Page 8 - admin audit log and break-glass
tasks.details: Screen 10. Actor, action, reason and before -> after on every override.
acceptanceCriteria: An override without a reason cannot be submitted
Every override appears in the audit table with its before/after
steps: Searchable audit table: actor, role, action, entity, reason, timestamp.
Expandable row showing the before/after jsonb diff.
Break-glass dialog on a study: choose the target status, type a mandatory reason, confirm.
Force-release-lock action with the same mandatory-reason dialog.
Make the destructive nature obvious - red confirm, owner named, no default selection.

tasks.title: Design pass against the mockups
tasks.details: The mockups are already designed - match them rather than inventing. Half a day here is what makes the demo look finished.
acceptanceCriteria: Screenshots of the running app are recognisably the mockups
No page shows a raw spinner-less blank state
steps: Pull the palette, IBM Plex type scale and the four status colours from MediView UI.dc.html.
Apply the dark reading view to the viewport page only; everything else stays light.
Add loading skeletons and empty states for all eight pages - an empty worklist should say so.
Check every page at 1440 and 1280 wide; desktop only, mobile is deferred.

sections.name: Audit, Break-glass & Security Pass
sections.goal: Days 42-43 - The healthcare-specific lesson, done properly but scoped: break-glass overrides that are always audited, and the four security checks worth doing. The v3 compliance programme (Key Vault, encryption at rest, GDPR tooling, PHI read-access logging) is deferred with the cloud deployment it belongs to.

tasks.title: Audit writes as a first-class part of the command
tasks.details: An audit row written by a middleware that guesses is worse than none. Write it in the handler where you know what actually changed.
acceptanceCriteria: An override and its audit row commit or roll back together
steps: Add an IAuditWriter port with Write(actor, action, entityType, entityId, reason, before, after).
Serialise before/after as jsonb from the projected DTO, never the whole entity.
Write the audit row in the same transaction as the change it describes.
Cover both actions: study.status.override and lock.force_release.

tasks.title: Force-release lock, end to end
tasks.details: The break-glass that unsticks a study when a doctor goes home with it open.
acceptanceCriteria: An admin can free a stuck study and the previous owner is told, live
The forced release is in the audit log with its reason
steps: Add ForceReleaseLockCommand behind AdminOnly with a mandatory reason.
Delete the Redis key regardless of the owner token, mark study_locks with release_reason admin_force, write the audit row.
Push LockReleased over SignalR so the previous owner's viewport goes read-only immediately.
Decide the study status: it stays in_progress - the read is unfinished, and an admin is not a doctor.

tasks.title: Prove the authorization boundary with tests
tasks.details: The one authorization rule that carries real meaning: an admin has nearly every power but cannot author a clinical record.
acceptanceCriteria: The authorization test suite is green and covers all three roles
steps: Write endpoint tests asserting an admin token gets 403 on create-draft, save-draft, add-medication and finalize.
Assert a patient token gets 403 on every doctor and admin endpoint.
Assert a doctor cannot fetch another patient's studies.
Assert a patient cannot fetch a study that is not theirs by guessing the id.

tasks.title: The four security checks worth doing now
tasks.details: Not a compliance programme - four concrete things that would each be a real bug.
acceptanceCriteria: No log statement contains a patient name
No secret or hash is returned by any endpoint
steps: Confirm no PHI in logs: grep the codebase for log statements that interpolate a name, DOB or report text.
Confirm passwords and refresh tokens are only ever stored hashed.
Confirm every ProblemDetails response in production hides exception details and stack traces.
Confirm the imaging retrieve endpoint requires authentication and note the deferred per-study authorization check in the ADR.

tasks.title: Write the deferred-scope ADR
tasks.details: Say out loud what you cut and why. In an educational project this document is worth as much as the code - it shows judgement, not just capability.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/adr/0001-mvp-scope.md exists and a reviewer can tell what was deliberate
steps: List every cut item from scope-cut.md with the reason and the re-entry cost.
For each, state what the design already accommodates - schemas, boundaries and events are unchanged.
Record the deliberate simplifications: snapshot columns instead of gRPC replicas, one report row per read instead of addenda, one role column instead of a permission matrix.

sections.name: Tests, Docs, Demo & Buffer
sections.goal: Days 44-45 - Make it provable and showable. Two days is not enough to retrofit testing, which is why the aggregate tests were written in their own sections - this block adds the integration layer, the docs and the demo, and keeps a real buffer.

tasks.title: One integration test per service with Testcontainers
tasks.details: A real Postgres in a container beats a mocked DbContext for anything involving a migration or a unique index.
acceptanceCriteria: `dotnet test` is green from a clean clone with Docker running
steps: Add Testcontainers.PostgreSql and a shared fixture that applies migrations to a throwaway database.
Identity: register -> login -> refresh. Studies: book -> import -> start read. Imaging: upload -> retrieve. Reporting: draft -> finalize.
Use WebApplicationFactory with the test container's connection string.
Keep them under a minute total or you will stop running them.

tasks.title: The end-to-end happy path test
tasks.details: One test that walks the entire product. If this is green, the project works.
acceptanceCriteria: The full journey passes in one automated run
steps: Register a patient, admin-create a doctor with a schedule, book a slot, import two DICOM files, doctor opens under lock, writes a report with a medication, finalizes with Done.
Assert the study ends at done, the lock is released and the patient can fetch the finalized report.
Run it against docker compose, not mocks.

tasks.title: GitHub Actions build and test workflow
tasks.details: Cut from the v3 plan: containerise, scan, push to ACR, migrate and deploy to Azure. Kept: the part that protects you daily.
acceptanceCriteria: A PR gets a green or red check within a few minutes
steps: Workflow on push and PR: setup .NET 10, restore, build with warnings-as-errors, run tests with the service containers.
Cache the NuGet packages.
Add a status badge to the README.
Do NOT add a deploy job - there is no cloud environment in this scope.

tasks.title: README, architecture doc and diagrams
tasks.details: The front door. Someone who has never seen the repo should be able to run it and understand it in fifteen minutes.
acceptanceCriteria: A stranger can clone, run and explain the system from the docs alone
steps: README: what it is, one screenshot of the viewport, the 6-line getting-started, the tech stack, the scope note.
docs/architecture.md: the four services, their schemas, the sync and async call paths, the lock design.
Regenerate the diagrams from static-graph so they show 4 services rather than 11.
Link mediview-mvp.dbml and scope-cut.md from the README.

tasks.title: Demo script and seeded demo data
tasks.details: Rehearse it. A five-minute walkthrough that shows the lock is the whole point of the project.
acceptanceCriteria: The demo runs start to finish from a freshly seeded database
steps: Write a seed command producing 2 doctors, 4 patients, 8 studies across all four statuses, and one study with real images.
Write the 5-minute script: patient books -> admin imports -> doctor A opens (lock) -> doctor B sees read-only -> A finalizes -> patient sees the result live.
Record it, or at least run it twice end to end without touching the database by hand.
Capture screenshots for the README while you are there.

tasks.title: Buffer and honest scope review
tasks.details: Reserve this. Something will overrun - it is usually Cornerstone or the outbox.
acceptanceCriteria: Nothing is half-finished and undocumented at day 45
steps: Re-read the deferred list and move anything you now consider essential in, cutting something else out.
Fix the top three rough edges you have been ignoring.
Write a short retrospective: what took longer than planned, and what you would cut first next time.
